explanation: Vietnamese public etiquette emphasizes modesty and avoiding behavior that draws attention, so openly blowing your nose in a crowd is generally seen as unrefined rather than strictly forbidden. The sources on Vietnamese manners do not address nose-blowing directly, so this verdict rests on the broader documented norm of public modesty and restraint. In practice, people tend to turn away or step aside rather than make a show of it.
local_tip: If you must clear your nose, turn away from others, use a tissue discreetly, and avoid loud honking sounds or inspecting the tissue afterward.

also_check.note: Blowing your nose loudly in public is frowned upon; sniffing or excusing yourself privately is preferred.
Public nose-blowing is common and tolerated, though spitting and loud clearing of the throat draw more disapproval.
Discreet nose-blowing with a tissue is acceptable, but loud or conspicuous blowing is considered poor manners.
